title: paged KV cache: block allocator reuse and pinning optimizations
author: Sofia Martinez
description: Motivation: reduce allocator churn and eviction thrashing in the paged KV cache under bursty generation loads. This PR implements allocator reuse, size-class freelists, and a soft pinning mechanism with TTL-based auto-unpin. These changes target two real issues observed in production: (1) high-frequency allocations causing fragmentation and lock contention on the BlockAllocator, and (2) hot-key eviction storms where recently-used KV blocks were being evicted and immediately reloaded, creating latency spikes. Summary: 1) BlockAllocator: introduce per-size-class freelists and a fast-path for reusing recently freed blocks (lock-free where possible), reduce cache-line bouncing, and batch reclamation of stale entries. 2) Reuse + Pinning: add a soft pin counter on blocks to allow short-term pinning of hot KV pages (used by continuous batching and long-running generation contexts) and a configurable TTL to automatically unpin after inactivity. 3) Eviction/GC: update eviction policy to skip pinned blocks, and add a fast fallback path that rotates candidate blocks to avoid O(N) scans. 4) Telemetry: new metrics for pin_count, allocator_hit_rate, per-size freelist depth, and eviction_skips; added traces around allocation and eviction hotspots. 5) Tests & Benchmarks: unit tests for allocator reuse and pin/unpin logic, integration tests under synthetic bursty workloads, and perf benchmark showing ~8-12% throughput improvement and 15-25% reduction in p99 tail latency for representative chat workloads. Compatibility: no public API changes; runtime config knobs added with sensible defaults. Rollout: feature gated and controlled by a runtime flag; default enabled for dedicated and private clusters after small canary. See linked Linear tickets for follow-ups.

release_notes: Performance: improved paged KV cache allocator reuse and pinning to reduce allocation churn and eviction-related latency spikes; adds new metrics (allocator_hit_rate, pin_count) and tuning docs. Default behavior is behind a runtime flag; enablement is planned via canary. Impact: ~8-12% throughput improvement and lower p99 tail latency for typical generation workloads.
notes_for_ops: Ops: default TTL for soft pinning is 30s; runtime flag 'kv_cache.allocator_reuse' controls feature.
